subject: Request: uplift to uptime target and pooled monthly remedy for migration month
messages:
From: Sophie Clarke <sophie.clarke@acmeco.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Engel <markus.engel@acmeco.com>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 14:12:00 +0100
Subject: Request: temporary uplift to uptime & pooled monthly remedy during migration

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As we scope our go-live we have one ask on the SLA that came up from our platform and finance teams: during our migration month (anticipated July window) we need a temporary uplift of the standard uptime target from 99.95% to 99.97% for our account, and — critically — we want the monthly remedy to be pooled across regions rather than capped per-region (our previous vendor offered an aggregated monthly cap).

Concretely:
- Uptime target: 99.97% (temporary for the migration month only)
- Remedy: allow aggregated monthly credit calculation across EU/US regions (instead of per-region caps) and raise the monthly maximum remedy from 50% invoice credit to 65% for that month only

We understand this is non-standard. If a migration window exception is possible we can align on a short addendum (1 month) and revert to standard SLA after. I attached a short note from AcmeCo finance and platform describing the rationale (AcmeCo_SLA_Request.pdf).

Can Redwood accommodate a one-month uplift + pooled remedy? If not, what’s the closest counterproposal you can offer? We’re on a tight procurement timeline and would like to finalize terms this week.

Best,
Sophie

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 09:37:00 -04:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: temporary uplift to uptime & pooled monthly remedy during migration

Forwarding AcmeCo ask — Sophie wants a one-month uplift to 99.97% and pooled monthly credits up to 65% for the migration month. They need terms this week.

Quoted for context:
> From: Sophie Clarke <sophie.clarke@acmeco.com>
> Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 14:12:00 +0100
> Subject: Request: temporary uplift to uptime & pooled monthly remedy during migration
>
> ... (see attached AcmeCo_SLA_Request.pdf)

My take / proposed counter (high level):
- Offer a timeboxed uplift to 99.96% (midpoint) for the migration month only, with clear rollback to 99.95% thereafter.
- For monthly remedy: allow aggregation across regions but cap the total monthly remedy at 60% of the invoice for that month (instead of their requested 65%). This preserves our exposure while addressing their consolidated-credit concern.
- Include mandatory migration controls: a) joint migration playbook, b) a single point SRE contact for weekly check-ins, c) a limited maintenance blackout during the migration window.
- Require a signed one-page addendum (we’ll produce the redline).

Risks/notes: full 99.97% is a material change to our availability commitments; legal will want a sunset and stronger force majeure/maintenance carveouts. We should also consider whether to restrict the uplift to specific service classes (e.g., hosted inference only).

If you agree I’ll draft a counter and attach a redlined SLA. Ben — raising this to Pricing to confirm the 60% cap is acceptable. Laura — can you prioritize a quick pass on the redline today?

Thanks,
Hannah

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Clarke <sophie.clarke@acmeco.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2026 15:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Proposed one-month SLA addendum for AcmeCo migration window

Hi Sophie — thanks for the patience while we reviewed this internally. Attached is a concise counterproposal and a redline of our standard SLA for your review (Redwood_SLA_Redline_v2.pdf). Summary of what we can do for the migration month: 

- Temporary uptime uplift: 99.96% for the migration month only (effective for the single calendar month covering the migration window).
- Remedy aggregation: we can permit pooled calculation of monthly remedies across regions, with the total monthly remedy capped at 60% of the invoice for that month (timeboxed for the migration month only).
- Preconditions: joint migration runbook, weekly status syncs with an assigned Redwood SRE, and a signed one-page addendum executed prior to the migration start date.
- Exclusions: standard maintenance carveouts apply; force majeure and network-provider events are excluded from remedy calculations.

We believe this is a balanced approach that reduces procurement friction while protecting both parties. If that’s acceptable I’ll route the addendum to Legal for signature and we can aim to have it in place before your migration.

Next steps:
- Sophie/Markus: confirm acceptance or propose any narrow edits by EOD Fri.
- Upon acceptance: we’ll drop in the addendum & produce the final signed PDF.

Best regards,
